description: REQ-120's own Edge Cases text (specs/behavioral-spec.md:120-125) states the 9000-block (~5h) lookback's only failure mode is that an operator 'risks missing a genuine on-chain reconciliation match for a row stuck longer than that window' -- this understates the ACTUAL consequence. Tracing resolveStaleProvisioning (lending-orchestrator.mjs:104-121): when reconcile() returns {found:false} for ANY reason (including a too-narrow window relative to when the real transfer actually landed), the code does not merely fail to help -- it AFFIRMATIVELY appends {...staleRow, status:'disbursement_failed'} and then PROCEEDS (runLockedIssuance step 6 onward) to attempt a FRESH disbursement to the SAME borrower with a NEW sequence number. If the original 'disbursement_uncertain' crash happened AFTER the facilitator genuinely broadcast+mined the transfer (the exact real-world failure mode this reconciliation exists to recover from -- e.g. a network timeout during waitForTransactionReceipt, not the privateKeyToAccount(undefined) pre-signing crash that happens to be today's specific loan_Franklin_1 symptom) and the NEXT reconciliation attempt for that lenderId happens more than ~5h (9000 blocks) after that broadcast, defaultReconcile will genuinely find nothing, mark the row disbursement_failed, and a fresh defaultDisburse call will send the SAME principal_usd to the SAME borrower a SECOND time -- an actual double-disburse of real money, not merely a 'permanently blocked lender' (which is the failure mode REQ-118b/REQ-120 were written to fix, but the fix as implemented trades an availability bug for a correctness bug). This is not merely hypothetical: skills/registry.json:93-102 declares economy/lending 'status:live' and reachable ONLY via the model-driven always-act menu (runtime/loop/always-act-router.mjs:27, DOCTRINE_EARN_ACTIONS -- 'economy/lending' is one of many earn actions the agent freely chooses among each wake, by design, per this repo's own no-hardcoded-judgment doctrine) -- there is NO engineered guarantee (fixed cron interval, a per-lender minimum-revisit SLA, or any code-level check) that a SPECIFIC lenderId's wake (and therefore its own stale-row reconciliation attempt) recurs within any bounded time of a prior crash. The reconciliation lookback is measured from 'now' (whenever that eventual re-attempt happens), never from staleRow.provisioned_ms -- there is no elapsed-time cross-check anywhere in resolveStaleProvisioning/defaultReconcile that would refuse (rather than silently conclude disbursement_failed) when (nowMs - staleRow.provisioned_ms) already exceeds what the lookback window can possibly cover.
specGap: specs/behavioral-spec.md:120-125 (REQ-120 Edge Cases) describes only the 'misses a match, lender blocked' consequence -- never states or mitigates the double-disburse consequence when the miss is a FALSE negative for a row that DID broadcast.
